{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
The church secretary kept finding 'accounting errors' that only she could fix, working late nights to correct them. She was celebrated for her dedication. An external audit found she'd been creating the errors herself—moving decimal points, then 'catching' them. She wanted to feel indispensable.

CANDIDATE A:
My uncle the plumber kept discovering pipe problems in his elderly mother's house that required his expertise. The family praised how devoted he was, always rushing over to save the day. After he died, another plumber found the pipes in perfect condition with fresh tool marks where 'problems' had been created. He'd manufactured emergencies so everyone would see him as indispensable.

CANDIDATE B:
The church secretary regularly found accounting errors made by volunteers and corrected them diligently. An external audit confirmed her catches were legitimate—volunteers had indeed made those mistakes. Her careful work saved the church from actual financial discrepancies.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:51"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both stories involve a character who creates problems to gain recognition and validation from others, ultimately revealing a deceptive need to feel indispensable."}
